title: Upsets Rock China Open as Sindhu, Shetty and Lakshya Lead India Into Last 16
excerpt: Denmark's Rasmus Gemke stuns world No. 2 Kunlavut Vitidsarn while three Indian singles players advance through a day of shocks at the BWF Super 1000 event in Changzhou.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rasmus Gemke stunned world No. 2 Kunlavut Vitidsarn in a thrilling upset at the China Open.
  • PV Sindhu advanced to the last 16 after defeating Unnati Hooda, setting up a clash with Chen Yufei.
  • Ayush Shetty and Lakshya Sen also progressed, defeating higher-ranked opponents in their matches.
  • India's doubles teams faced early exits, missing key players due to injury.
Upsets Shake Up the Draw
›Rasmus Gemke defeated Kunlavut Vitidsarn (21-13, 8-21, 21-19)
›Li Shifeng lost to Nhat Nguyen (12-21, 21-14, 18-21)
›Sindhu beat Unnati Hooda (21-14, 9-21, 21-10)
›Ayush Shetty upset Alwi Farhan (21-17, 5-21, 21-17)
›Lakshya Sen defeated Yushi Tanaka (22-20, 15-21, 21-14)

Seeds Fall in Changzhou

The second day of the BWF China Open 2026 in Changzhou delivered a string of upsets that reshaped the men's singles draw and underlined the rising depth of talent beyond the sport's traditional powerhouses.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZ1UUacCBFt/

The most dramatic result came when Denmark's Rasmus Gemke, ranked 30th in the world, dismantled second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn of Thailand 21-13, 8-21, 21-19. Gemke dominated the opener with a late surge of seven consecutive rallies, surrendered the second game comprehensively, then held his nerve through a tense decider that reached 19-all before he converted his only match point with a leaping smash.

"Being aggressive was my only chance — try to win the points quickly and make him a little uncomfortable. I think I succeeded with that. Today's my day and I'm so proud of my performance."

— Rasmus Gemke, after defeating world No. 2 Vitidsarn

It was Gemke's first victory over a top-five player since beating Li Shifeng at the 2023 China Masters, and his first win over the former world champion and Olympic silver medallist in three years. He will face France's Toma Junior Popov in the second round.

China's seventh seed Li Shifeng fell next, losing 12-21, 21-14, 18-21 to Ireland's Nhat Nguyen in their fourth career meeting. Nguyen, ranked 24th, had never beaten the Chinese star before.

"For Ireland to beat China, for me, it's a big deal. I've always wanted to compete against the best, so doing this gives me a lot of motivation that players from small countries can overcome the cream of the crop."

— Nhat Nguyen, after his maiden win over Li Shifeng

India's Singles Stars Advance

While the seeds tumbled, India's top three singles players navigated a challenging day to reach the round of 16.

PV Sindhu, riding a wave of confidence after winning the Japan Open title last week, overcame fellow Indian Unnati Hooda 21-14, 9-21, 21-10 in 56 minutes. The two-time Olympic medallist avenged her defeat to the 18-year-old at the same tournament last year, reasserting control in a dominant third game after losing the second. Sindhu now faces a high-profile clash against fourth seed Chen Yufei of China — a player she defeated during her Japan Open title run.

Ayush Shetty produced one of the day's standout results, knocking out Indonesia's world No. 11 Alwi Farhan 21-17, 5-21, 21-17. The young Indian has established himself as a genuine giant-killer this season, having also upset world No. 7 Li Shifeng at the Badminton Asia Championships in April. He will next face Nguyen, the Irishman who eliminated Li Shifeng earlier in the day.

Lakshya Sen completed India's singles sweep with a hard-fought 22-20, 15-21, 21-14 victory over Japan's Yushi Tanaka, recovering after a tight opening game and a setback in the second to dominate the decider with powerful smashes. He meets Canada's Victor Lai in the next round.

Doubles Disappointment for India
›Men's doubles: Amsakarunan/Ramachandran lost to Liang/Wang (16-21, 7-21)
›Mixed doubles: Kapoor/Gadde lost to Feng/Huang (9-21, 16-21)
›Star pair Rankireddy/Shetty withdrew due to injury.
›Indonesia's women's doubles pair defeated China's second seeds.

Doubles Disappointment for India

India's doubles campaign fared less well. Men's doubles pair Hariharan Amsakarunan and Arjun Madathil Ramachandran were outclassed 21-16, 21-7 by China's fourth seeds Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang. In mixed doubles, Rohan Kapoor and Ruthvika Shivani Gadde lost 21-9, 21-16 to China's top-seeded pair Feng Yanzhe and Huang Dongping. India is missing the star pairing of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who withdrew as Rankireddy continues recovering from a shoulder injury.

The doubles upsets were not limited to Indian pairs. Indonesia's Rachel Allessya Rose and Febi Setianingrum avenged their Japan Open loss by defeating China's second-seeded women's doubles pair Jia Yifan and Zhang Shuxian 24-22, 21-17 in just 37 minutes.

What's Next

The round of 16 matches on Thursday set up several compelling storylines. Sindhu's encounter with Chen Yufei is the headline act, a rematch of their Japan Open meeting that could signal whether the Indian star's late-career resurgence is the real thing. Shetty faces Nguyen in a contest between two of the day's most impressive performers, while Sen will look to maintain his form against Lai.

The China Open, a BWF Super 1000 event, carries significant ranking points ahead of the 2026 World Championships in New Delhi in August — a home event where India will be desperate to medal. The tournament concludes on Sunday in Changzhou, Jiangsu Province.
